name: Tunisian Brik
description: Real brik à l'oeuf, the classic version served in nearly every Tunis restaurant, has a specific filling of mashed potato, tuna, capers, onion, and parsley, with a raw egg cracked into a well right before folding - traditional malsouka pastry is round and hand-pressed on a hot dome, thinner and more delicate than phyllo, but phyllo is the standard, widely available substitute even among Tunisian cooks abroad. The yolk staying soft inside the crackling-crisp shell is the entire point, not a mistake to fix.

steps_detailed: Mix the mashed potato, tuna, capers, onion, and cilantro together.
Spoon the mixture onto a phyllo sheet, make a well in the center, and crack the egg into it.
Fold into a triangle immediately, sealing the edges carefully so the yolk stays intact - the raw egg white helps seal the pastry as you fold.
Fry immediately, 1-2 minutes per side, just until the pastry is golden and crisp - the yolk should still be soft and runny inside.

name: Tunisian Couscous
description: Tunisian couscous is genuinely more assertively spicy than its Algerian and Moroccan neighbors, built on real harissa in the broth rather than just warming spices - real technique steams the couscous two or three separate times, fluffing between each round, which is what builds properly light, separate grains rather than a dense clump.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

ingredients.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

steps_detailed: Simmer the chicken, carrot, chickpeas, and harissa seasoning in 1.5 cups water 25-28 minutes until the chicken is tender.
Toss the dry couscous with the olive oil and a splash of water, rubbing between your hands to coat every grain.
Steam the couscous over the simmering stew for 10 minutes, then fluff and rub with wet hands to break up clumps.
Steam a second time for 8-10 minutes, fluffing again - this real double-steam builds properly light, separate grains.
Serve the stew and broth over the finished couscous.
